plan.title: The Leash 5 — Mercer resurfaces at the Undertow (BUILT rev 117; the new name, and she doesn't use it)
canvases: cap_mercer_resurfaces (auto-fire @underworld_bar, pri 11, one-shot, gated print_needed is_true + mercer_found is_false). NO requires_npc — deliberate, see the schedule note below; shipped precedent is salvage_relaunch @the_waterfront, a whole Mercer canvas at a location he has no row for. 14 cascade beats / 13 visible clicks, 445 words, 0.93:1, Tier-3 CAPSTONE and the cap_ prefix is EARNED (beat_0071 declined the badge and dropped its prefix; this one keeps both, and check 5 passes on beat count, not on a declaration). SETS mercer_found; exits back to underworld_bar, +30 min.

THE ORDER IS THE BEAT. Sight first — she places him at the end table before he knows she is there. Then DELIGHT, undefended: out of the chair, both hands, 'Wren — look at you', and he is holding on rather than checking her over. Only a beat later, lowered to the level the corners use, ask #1 of three, played as a JOKE: 'It's Adler. Adler, all right? Humour an old man his fresh coat of paint.' AND SHE DOESN'T STOP — 'What are you doing down here, Mercer.' in the very next breath, and the scene does not comment; he waits half a second for something to follow it and nothing does. He cannot get properly angry, because she isn't defying him: she just hasn't changed, which is exactly what she has always been to him. ONE flat thought_bubble ('She notices that she said it twice and didn't stop when he asked. She files it with the readings and doesn't look at it again.'). The terminal beat puts his HANDS on the table — soft, a signet he's stopped wearing, the pale band still on the finger — and she does not tell him why she came.

⚠️ THE NEW NAME IS ASSERTED STRUCTURALLY, NOT BY STRING COUNT. My first live check asserted 'appears exactly once' and FAILED at count=2 — his line says it twice ('It's Adler. Adler, all right?'), which is right for a man pleading and wrong for that assertion. The rule that actually matters is that it never reaches NARRATION or HER mouth, so the test was rebuilt to walk every block of the merged TOML and require that each block carrying the name is a dialog with speaker=npc + npcId=npc_mercer. A flat text count cannot tell narration from dialogue, and narration is the thing that must never carry it.

⚠️ THE ENGINE-FORCED SHAPE — mercer_room + his second schedule row, and why the Undertow could not hold it. A [[npcs.schedules]] row CANNOT be conditional: the resolver reads exactly five keys (location/weekdays/start_time/end_time/activity, v2.py:979-985) and silently drops anything else, and getNpcLocation walks rows FIRST-MATCH-WINS in declaration order (v2.py:3439-3454). Mercer's Act-1 penthouse row (08:00-23:00) is therefore permanent — and it STAYS, because cap_first_penthouse_service (5_scenes:23) and mercer_penthouse_hub (:73) both carry requires_npc='npc_mercer', so removing it would kill live content and orphan a returning player mid-Act-1. That leaves any new row owning only 23:00-08:00. THEN THE REAL PROBLEM: presence has two surfaces and only one is canvas-gated. The in-room portrait card is (v2.py:4998-5008), but the NAV-CARD BADGE is not — getNpcsPresentAtLocation (v2.py:4773) is pure schedule occupancy with no canvas gate and no hidden_from_ui filter. A row at the public underworld_bar would therefore park Mercer's face on the Undertow's nav card every night FROM ACT 1b ONWARD, before he is blown and before she has found him, spoiling the one beat this chapter turns on. THE WAY OUT IS IN THE SAME CODE: the indicators block lives only in the open_card branch; locked_card renders image + name + reason and NOTHING else (v2.py:19270-19281 — verified in the shipped output/index.html, not just the generator source). So his only underworld row is at mercer_room, locked on mercer_found. Leak zero, and live-verified in BOTH directions: badges:0 while locked, badges:1 once mercer_found opens it.

TWO CONSEQUENCES, BOUGHT ON PURPOSE. (1) MERCER IS A NIGHT NPC. Kess's yard is 10:00-22:00 and Mercer owns the complement, so the chapter splits clean — day is the bench, night is the man — and the whole loop (beats 0074, 0076-0079) is night work. (2) NO PORTRAIT HUB AT THE BAR: the engine hard-refuses a clickable portrait to an NPC it cannot place at the location, so beat_0073's hub_mercer_undertow is RE-SHAPED from a portrait hub to a plain location canvas. His face lands at hub_mercer_room instead, which is where the escalation actually happens; Sol and Colm keep theirs at the bar. Both consequences bounced UP to the design book (blueprint rows 6, 6b, 6c, 7 + the header changelog) rather than being worked around in TOML.

'The Lockup' is named to be TRUE IN BOTH ERAS. The greyed card sits on the market's nav grid from the moment the underworld opens in Act 1b — long before Mercer is blown — and a location's display name cannot be re-cut later without breaking the fiction twice. So it is ordinary rented storage behind the stalls: scenery before the reveal, his after it. Nothing in the name or the blocked_message ('Somebody rents it and keeps it bolted. Not a door that opens for the curious.') names him, hints at him, or reads as a held door. It also stays clear of Colm's back room and Bastien's (beat_0082). ⚠️ entry_conditions carries version='1.0' or the lock FAILS OPEN with no build error.

QUEST CARD G (mercer_found is_true + owner_print_taken is_false) — and it is not bookkeeping. mercer_found CLOSES card F, and the chapter's next Story-Goal card is not authored until beat_0084, so without G the Story-Goals spine would sit BLANK for twelve beats of live play — the whole Mercer arc, the loop, and Bastien. That is the same defect class beat_0071 had to correct a turn late; caught in planning this time. G follows the D/E/F shape (prior-stage flag is_true + this-stage completion flag is_false) and carries the build boundary + the Support-Us ask forward. F KEEPS its copy of the ask rather than handing it over — the rev-113 precedent set on D, so a player who stops at any rung still sees it — and F's boundary sentence stays true where it stands, so nothing in F had to be re-cut. owner_print_taken is not SET until beat_0074; quest `when` has no validation site, so this builds green and an unset flag reads is_false, which is exactly the wanted behaviour.

§7 AUDITS: check 5 PASS (declared CAPSTONE, 14 beats, >=10) · check 2 PASS after TWO FORCED SPLITS — the first draft ran beat 0 at 61w and beat 6 at 51w, and doctrine says a beat over ~50 wanted to be two beats, so both were SPLIT, never compressed (new max 48w, average ~32; beats 4 and 6 sit deliberately bare at 12w and 19w because the refusal has to land as nothing) · check 3 PASS 0.93:1 canvas, 1.04:1 counting thought_bubble · check 1 PASS 0 second-person leaks · canvas total 445w inside the 400-800 Tier-3 budget · whole game 3.23 -> 3.17:1.

That is what makes him sit down and it is why the scene needs no threat to be frightening. REV 67b — THE GATE OWNS ITS CAR (LO caught it: 'Under world take car should give two options right, spire and waterfront, currently it shows spire and underworld'). He was right, and it exposed that my rev-67 'correction' was itself half-wrong. THE BUG: the gate had no car of its own — it INHERITED the waterfront's activity_travel_to_spire via parent, and canvas inheritance copies an ancestor's canvas VERBATIM (v2.py walks the parent chain collecting every canvas triggered at each ancestor). So the gate showed the WATERFRONT's menu: 'Ride up to the Spire' (fine) + 'Down under the docks — the Underworld' (a no-op — she is STANDING in the underworld), and could not offer the Reach (pointless from the waterfront, which is where that canvas lives). No per-canvas opt-out exists, and the engine has NO player-location condition (only npc_at_location, engine-reference:315) — so a shared menu cannot adapt to where it renders. MY ERROR: at rev 67 I offered to build exactly this picker, then CANCELLED it after seeing 'Take the car (from The Waterfront)' at the gate and declaring 'it already exists'. It existed with the wrong menu — the live render was literally showing me the '(from The Waterfront)' parenthetical and I read the words, not the meaning. Second instance in one session of reading the first thing and stopping (cf. getNpcsWithSchedules, where I read loop 1 and missed loop 2). THE FIX: (1) NEW canvas activity_travel_from_gate @ underworld_gate, pri 2, repeatable — 'Ride up to the Spire.' -> spire_plaza (30 min) / 'Up to the Reach.' -> the_waterfront (10 min). Time only, no Charge (rev 67 doctrine). (2) underworld_gate DROPS parent AND entry_from. parent bought nothing once the gate owns its car, and it cost THREE leaks: captivity_recovery / salvage_body_wont_hold / salvage_relaunch are one-shots scoped '@the_waterfront' and were inheriting down to the gate too. entry_from was already inert under auto_exit and the gate has no entry_conditions, so the passage guard never needs its go-back target. The rev-67 comment saying 'KEEP parent — it inherits the car' is CORRECTED in place. INVARIANTS HELD (all live-verified): she still CANNOT walk in — with no entry_from the gate is nobody's child so it never lands on the waterfront's nav grid; auto_exit=false still suppresses the list-every-location fallback, and is now doing the WHOLE job (the Leave link is gone with entry_from, so only the fallback half is load-bearing here). WORK THE CASE — state-aware status ladder + the ENGINE FACT that adjacent group ladders MERGE. LO: 'Work on case' confuses players into working more and more; it should say where the case stands, hint when more work IS needed, and say plainly when it isn't. Correct, and worse than 'no hint': case_progress has exactly THREE consumers game-wide (cap_case_insider >=2, cap_case_curated >=4, cap_case_pipe >=6) and nothing reads it above 6, while relation's only gate anywhere is >=15 (the access capstone) — so past pipe_known every 60-minute session paid literally NOTHING and the exit still read 'Keep at it.' The base node's only [group] axis was calloway_drains_done (pre/post drain), so the prose was byte-identical at 0 boxes and at 20. Third defect: reveal #3 double-locks on case_progress>=6 AND calloway_believes, so a player who worked but never talked was short on TRUST, not boxes — and more work was the only verb the room suggested. FIX (5_scenes.toml, work_the_case only): a 6-band status ladder on the base node keyed to the case chain — 1 nothing read yet / 2 has the how, needs the hand / 3 THE WRONG-VERB RESCUE (blocker is his trust, not boxes) / 4 sealed side open, far end close / 5 EXHAUSTED, the name was never written down, that answer's in the Reach / 6 rogue known, it's Vane two desks away. Bands 5-6 point OUT of the room, which is what LO asked for. Exit text 'Keep at it.' -> 'Log the hour.' (neutral, stops arguing with the status line). Ported from activity_yard_crawl's yard_depth ladder, exhausted line included. Activity deliberately NOT retired (it's her cover; the post-drain body variant is authored) — it tells the truth about being spent instead. ⚠️ ENGINE FACT LEARNED THE HARD WAY: the generator collapses CONSECUTIVE group blocks into ONE <<if>>/<<elseif>>/<</if>> chain (v2.py:13649-13662 collects the run, _render_group_chain builds it). The first build compiled all EIGHT groups (2 body + 6 status) into a single exclusive chain, so a body band always matched first and the six status bands were DEAD CODE — build green, validator green, zero warnings, silently wrong. A non-group block between them starts a NEW chain, so the two ladders are separated by a real transitional line ('She squares the pulled boxes back into the row and marks the hour on his sheet.') carrying a DO-NOT-DELETE comment. Audited both games for the same signature (group runs whose conditions split into disjoint key-sets): 0 elsewhere — this pattern was attempted nowhere else. VERIFIED: build green (validation OK / Validation passed / All flag chains valid / Package ready; 12 pre-existing extractor warnings unchanged; placeholders now 0 IMAGE + 0 VIDEO MISSING — the 6 Colm slots got filled). Playwright: all 6 states show their own band and NONE of the other five, with the correct pre/post-drain body alongside; exit renders 'Log the hour.' and clicks through to Location_vance_securities; case_progress 0->1, relation 0->3, hour 12->13 (location-exit effects apply at canvas RENDER, not on the click — 'you saw it' semantics); and selectAutoFireCanvasForLocation still returns cap_case_insider / cap_case_curated / cap_case_pipe at case_progress 2/4/6, proving the ladder is display-only.

beat_0076 BUILT + GREEN — the parts loop spends for the first time, and it fails. No ceiling work was needed: the row this beat spends is Mercer's, signed at rev 119, and its clause (iii) explicitly held the anal back FOR THE LOOP. So the anal lands here, and it lands for a reason rather than as an escalation — mercer_finisher (Act 1, shipped) already canonises that his anal finish passes nothing to her ('No give, no opening, no man-belonging-to-her. The same nothing as every time'), so the reach rides exactly the act where her body has spent two years finding nothing. That is what makes try 1's identical nothing cruel: she has had a thing cut into her spine specifically to change that moment and the moment is unchanged. THE ONE STRUCTURAL CALL, surfaced rather than patched in quietly: blueprint scene 13 placed the four attempts as one canvas with an exclusive banded [group] chain, and the [group] chain is wrong here. One canvas is right and it stays one canvas. But a band is the right tool for a one- or two-line variant — which is exactly what Kess's build talk on the install is, and those stay bands — and the wrong tool for a variant that is four to six beats with its own cascade, because §7 check 2 folds the entire node lead into beat 0's measured unit and four multi-beat bands there measure as a single ~250-word beat even though exactly one renders. Per-generation nodes, routed by mutually exclusive choice conditions on mercer_attempts, give each try its own exit, beat count and word budget, and they sidestep the adjacent-[group] merge trap instead of managing it. The design book, the blueprint note under the table and design_the_leash §8 and §16 all carry the correction. THE SECOND CALL is the first time beat_0075's render-time finding has changed an authoring decision rather than a test assertion: the burn and the bump ride the ROUTING CHOICE, not a node exit, because a choice's effects fire on click while an exit block's fire on render. Live-verified in both directions — after the whole evening has rendered and been clicked through, the part is still seated and no attempt is banked; the click moves both. The rung's gate widens one notch per beat so the loop can never route into a try node that does not exist yet, which is stricter than the install's fence on purpose: a missing line of Kess's is a hole, but a missing try node would be the whole sex scene with no result. BAND 1 OF THE INSTALL landed, discharging the debt beat_0075 owed forward, and it forced a measured constraint worth carrying: every band from here has to be 21 words or fewer, because beat 0's max reading is lead 29 plus the longest single band and that is now exactly 50. Both this canvas and the attempt's four-line block_pool are measured max-not-sum, documented in their headers rather than bent down to satisfy an arithmetic that does not describe what renders. A TOOL GAP was found and closed: audit_s7.py's beat_units() only ever walked nodes[0], so a canvas that routes variants into sibling nodes had its per-beat density silently unmeasured; it now takes an optional node index and .try1 measures clean at 36 w max. THE SKILL WAS FIXED AT THE CLASS LEVEL. Two gaps, both found by reading the generator this turn. (1) engine-reference §3 documented every TemplateChoice key and never said what happens when NO choice passes — the engine emits a console.warn, a $flags.debug_mode diagnostic listing every failed predicate, and a player-facing Continue escape that fires no effects (v2.py:12890-12946). Without that, an author either adds a redundant fallback choice that then double-renders or avoids conditional routing entirely. (2) The skill named the adjacent-[group] merge trap once, in system-patterns.md, and never taught the positive alternative — multi-beat variants belong in per-variant NODES routed by exclusive choice conditions; [group] bands are for one- and two-line variants — which is the exact call this beat had to make, and I planned the wrong shape first and only caught it against the audit's own arithmetic. No new flags, no new traits, no quest work (card I already spans the whole loop by design). Media debt 9 -> 11. Playwright 56/56 plus 65/65, 46/46, 51/51 and 34/34 regressions; beat_0075's in-progress assertion about the missing band was retargeted rather than deleted, and its band-count structural check was rewritten to hold at any band count. Whole game 2.88 -> 2.84:1. Nothing committed, nothing released.

beat_0077 BUILT + GREEN — try 2, it bites back, and the leash finally got a ceiling row of its own. THE CEILING FIRST, because it was the blocker and it was a real one rather than a formality. The three signed rows each govern a PERSON'S register — Mercer's what he does (unchanged and correct here), Kess's what his hands do, Bastien's what he says — and none of them reaches HER BODY ACTING ON ITS OWN, which is the entire content of try 2. I measured before drafting rather than asserting: across the whole 5_scenes.toml there were exactly two pieces of pain-register prose, the cell's overflow (which the captivity re-spec scopes to captive_room and states in those words) and kess_install_part saying explicitly that what she feels is NOT pain. So damage to her outside that room had never shipped, and try 2 does. LO signed the drafted row: the clamp is DAMAGE AND NOT SEXUAL (no forced orgasm, no arousal, no ecstasy-as-damage — the governor is 'design, not damage' in salvage_verdict's own words, and a guard bites the way a machine bites); the captivity re-spec is NOT widened (one event, once, no pack, no restraint, Tier-3 zero); THE CHARGE IS CONCEALMENT, NOT PAIN, with pain-as-spectacle named as the failure mode; and one thought_bubble, observing. The row covers try 3 as well, so it was signed once instead of twice and beat_0078 has no ceiling block. THE SCENE'S ENGINE is the thing worth carrying forward: it works without a fail branch because the half of the clamp MERCER CAN FEEL — her body gripping down on him — is the exact thing he has always wanted from her, so he misreads it as her finally responding and is delighted. She never has to hide that half. What she hides is everything else, and the near-miss is him noticing she is shaking and accepting 'It's cold in here', because looking at her face would cost him an effort he has not spent in two years. That is what keeps it a scene about her getting away with something rather than a scene about her being hurt, which is exactly what clause (iii) asks for. ONE CORRECTION, surfaced not patched: §9's sketch put the clamp MID-FUCK and it lands AT THE HOLD. Structurally it has to — the shared .base node ends with him finishing and holding, and the reach IS the routing click, so nothing can land earlier without banding the shared node, which is the shape beat_0076 struck. It is also better there: while he is fucking her he is moving and loud and self-absorbed, and at the hold he is still and quiet and against her. Both the chapter file and the design book's mirrored paragraph carry the correction, and while the design book's chapter section was under the pen its stale try-1 sketch ('on her back', 'a thing in her chest') was fixed too — beat_0076 corrected that in design_the_leash §9 and the review surface had been left contradicting it. THE ONE SILENT-FAILURE GUARD went in as planned: hub_mercer_room's rung gate widened lt 1 -> lt 2 in the same edit as the node. It fails silently in both directions with a green build, so it is asserted from both sides. FOUR FRONTIER ASSERTIONS in the 0075 and 0076 suites were RETARGETED rather than deleted, and three of them rewritten to DERIVE the frontier — the node count, the routing-choice count, the band count and the hub gate now assert the invariant (band 0 is lt 1, every later band is a clean [gte n, lt n+1], the try nodes follow the shared evening in order, the gate equals the number of authored try nodes) instead of a fixed number. A guard that needs a hand-edit every beat is a guard that eventually gets hand-edited to match the bug. And one test bug is worth recording as a class: the ceiling assertion counted thought_bubbles by regexing for '"thought_bubble"' over str(dict), and repr() of a dict uses SINGLE quotes, so it matched nothing. beat_0081 BUILT + GREEN — the back room and the search at the door, and THE LAST UNSIGNED CEILING ROW IS SIGNED. The buyer wanted what was DONE to her rather than what she can do, and asked one question twice, was she made or was she taken. What ships is a two-condition contract that teaches itself: the shipped loop already teaches only the anal finish opens the drain, and Bastien adds and only with the key running; anal with the key asleep routes to the cold-socket nothing, no bump and no fail screen. beat_0083 BUILT + GREEN — the extraction, and THE CHAPTER'S CONTENT IS COMPLETE. decisions_log: beat_0084 (rev 129, 2026-08-11) — THE QUESTS PAGE, READ END TO END. The spine passed: one live Story-Goal at every state, D through M, M alone after leash_cut. Three things did not. (1) Cards E, F and G still claimed the build ends at them; the claim is global and cannot be checked locally, which is why the per-card check passed three times. Now exactly one card names it; the Support-Us ask rides every rung and card H got its own back. (2) The NPC tier was authored against Act 1a's map — the 1a close seals the Spire, so Calloway's ladder and half of Colm's end card pointed at an unreachable floor, while Renner's section vanished on his own drain even though his office stays open. (3) The chapter had no NPC tier at all: Mercer and Bastien, the two conquests it runs on, had nothing. rev 130 (2026-08-11) — THE PARTS LOOP WAS CORRECT AND UNREADABLE, AND THE rev-129 SWEEP WAS A HALF-SWEEP. Out of beat sequence, and correctly so: LO playtested and stalled — he bought the part and the game stopped. Reproduced live against the built game: NO logic bug, NO soft-lock, every gate doing exactly what its TOML says, and the lapse always recoverable because the cot is a Wren-solo activity with no presence gate. Three gates were stacked and none was visible: the install rung hides on a lapsed feed line, the spend rung hides when the part is bought but not seated, and Kess (10:00-22:00) and Mercer's Lockup (23:00-08:00) have ZERO overlapping hours across the whole 24 — measured, not inferred — so one cycle is necessarily two trips and nothing said so. FIXED IN PROSE, NOT MENUS: hub_kess_berth goes from two upkeep bands to four (feed_line_days x part_held; the new lapsed-and-carrying band is the only place in the game connecting the part in her pocket to the bill, and it names the cot), hub_mercer_room splits its is_true band so an unseated part is stated in the room, both off-hours cards give the hours as hours, and card I's tip says the cycle takes two trips. show_when_locked CANNOT do this job — it greys on a choice's WHOLE conditions block (v2.py:12798), so it is all-or-nothing and would advertise the loop from the moment the canvas exists; the original hide-don't-grey call was right and the missing half was the prose. ENGINE: the Schedules page was still resolving Mercer to the penthouse — sealed by this chapter's own opening flag — for fifteen hours of every twenty-four, with his real address as the inactive row, plus Calloway and Vane parked in Vance Securities. Schedule rows carry no conditions and cannot (the resolver reads five keys and drops the rest), so :: SchedulePage now checks navDestUnlocked per row, mutes unreachable rows with navDestBlockedReason, and suppresses the NOW badge for a locked location. Found on the way: class="<<print _rowClass>>" was never evaluated — SugarCube emits macros inside a raw HTML attribute verbatim — so the current-slot highlight had been dead since it shipped; both rows now use @class. SKILL: lanes.md gains the second half of hide-don't-grey (hide a story gate, SPEAK an upkeep gate, and speak it in a prose band) plus the note that banding a base node on a recoverable state is not the banned opener-tiering; quests.md §10 gains the surface table (quest cards / Schedules page / off-hours cards / hub prose) and a live-read step, because no grep catches staleness produced at render time. VERIFIED: merge --validate OK, package exit 0, check_cascade_order exit 0, check_render_buckets flags only react_renner_threat; repro_parts_stall.py 33/33 live; regression suites 0072-0084 re-run. TWO SUITES WERE CORRECTED RATHER THAN RE-PINNED: live_beat_0076.py:294 hard-coded a band count of 2 as a proxy for the adjacent-[group] chain being well-formed, so a correct edit failed a guard that was counting instead of checking — it now asserts the invariant (chain opens on the is_false band, ENDS on the bare is_true catch-all, every band between is strictly narrower). live_beat_0073.py:236 was RIGHT and was obeyed: it forbids any thought_bubble on Mercer's surfaces (beat_0073's authored silence), so the Mercer read-out was rewritten from her interior into third-person narration of her body. LEFT OPEN, SURFACED NOT FIXED: vance_securities has two gates in two acts and one blocked_message written for the first, so a 1b player reads the muted row's reason as 'Mercer hasn't sent her up there yet', which is the wrong lock — still strictly better than the page saying 'go here now', but it wants a message true in both phases or a per-clause reason, and that is a design call. Also noted: prose assertions must not read --debug placeholder text — live_beat_0074.py's anal-hold check trips on a media description's 'avoid: ... anal' clause when the build carries --debug, and passes 46/46 without it. Nothing renamed, re-gated shut or removed.

(2) THE EMITTER HAD BEEN DEAD SINCE THE 1a CLOSE, and this is a new failure shape: A REACHABLE GATE WITH AN UNREACHABLE SETTER. activity_recharge_emitter is @cradle and activity_swap_weapon is @wren_room, both Spire-side and route-cut by archive_1a_done. (3) The object she buys four times had no NAME — 'a part', 'a build', 'small dead components' everywhere. It is a TALKBACK now, in Kess's mouth at kess_print_read, at the stall, and in card I's tip. ⚠️ HALF OF LO'S THIRD NOTE WAS WRONG AND WAS NOT BUILT: he asked whether kess_print_read 'names and logically reasons' the part. The reasoning was always there and is thorough (live rather than played back, from where the challenge is asked i.e. at the seam, a part a go off the small stalls not the blades, and he won't guess how many). Only the naming was missing. ⚠️ AND DELIBERATELY UNANSWERED: whether the scene says the controller hears and sees what Wren does. It does not. That is a lore decision about what the chip is, it connects to LO's older chairman/memory-transmitter sketch, and the resequencing beat reworks the controller anyway — it needs his call, not a guess. SKILL: lanes.md gains the third failure under the terminal-flag sweep — a region sealing is not a terminal flag and retires nothing, so the existing audit ('does this gate still have a true branch?') passes clean while a mechanic's only maintenance surface dies inside the seal.
